theater: 塞維亞、加的斯與馬德里

battle.name: 西班牙立憲革命
battle.theater: 塞維亞、加的斯與馬德里
battle.brief: 一八二〇年一月一日，拉斐爾·德·列戈在塞維亞舉起一八一二年憲法，逼斐迪南七世宣誓；加的斯、巴塞羅那、馬德里響應，國王三月九日屈服。一八二二年七月皇軍反攻奪回馬德里，一八二三年法軍越比利牛斯入境，五月二十日占領都城，立憲派退守加的斯，列戈十一月被絞。燧發槍是兩方步兵骨幹。

kit.name: 燧發槍
kit.history: 擊錘打火比火繩穩。線性列陣的射速和精度都靠它撐著。

countries: 交戰是西班牙國內兩種政治勢力的正面對撞：國王斐迪南七世一方是正統派，王權、教會與一八一四年復辟後重新設立的宗教裁判所構成其骨幹，駐軍中的皇室衛隊與各省的「王室義勇兵」是它的武裝；另一方是立憲派，骨幹是受過拿破崙戰爭洗禮、對一八一二年《加的斯憲法》抱有認同的陸軍軍官與城市國民警衛隊，一八二〇年初各城市的洪都拉斯與志願民兵在暗中串聯。法國不是交戰方，而是以神聖同盟的名義出兵干預：維羅納會議授權法國出兵，昂古萊姆公爵率「聖路易的十萬子孫」自北面進入伊比利亞半島；俄羅斯、奧地利與普魯士保留在神聖同盟的名義上而不派一兵，英國外相卡寧公開反對干預，威靈頓在巴黎拒絕讓英軍參與，荷蘭與普魯士同樣不派兵，因此一八二三年的戰場上只有法國一國的軍隊在打西班牙人。西班牙本身的指揮系統是各軍區總司令與軍部：安達盧西亞、卡塔隆尼亞、阿拉貢與納瓦拉各有總司令，自由派另設「內陸軍」，由埃斯波斯·伊·米納統率；正統派方面則有宮廷樞密、主教與一八二二年自行組成的王室義勇兵隊伍。
countriesEn: The fighting was a head-on collision between two political forces inside Spain. On the side of King Fernando VII stood the absolutists: the crown, the Church and the Spanish Inquisition re-established after the restoration of 1814 formed the backbone, and the Royal Guard in the garrisons and the royalist volunteers of the provinces provided the arms. On the other side stood the constitutionalists, whose core was made up of army officers and city militia who had been through the Peninsular War and felt an affinity with the Constitution of Cadiz of 1812; in the early months of 1820 the juntas of the cities and the volunteer militia were in secret correspondence with one another. France was not a belligerent but the power that intervened in the name of the Holy Alliance: the Congress of Verona authorised the expedition, and the Duke of Angoulême led the Hundred Thousand Sons of Saint Louis into the Iberian Peninsula from the north; Russia, Austria and Prussia kept the name of the Holy Alliance without sending a single man, the British foreign secretary Canning opposed the intervention openly, Wellington refused in Paris to let British troops take part, and neither the Netherlands nor Prussia sent troops either, so that in the field in 1823 a single country's army was fighting the Spanish. Spain's own chain of command ran through the captain-generals of the armies and the war ministry: Andalusia, Catalonia, Aragon and Navarre each had a captain-general, while the constitutionalists raised a separate Interior Army under Francisco Espoz y Mina; on the absolutist side stood the privy councillors of the court, the bishops and the royalist volunteer bands that formed themselves in 1822.
people: 引火者拉斐爾·德·列戈是加拉尼加斯人，一八〇八年因反對法軍入侵而首次入獄，獲釋後在軍中以敢言聞名，一八一九年至一八二〇年間在軍官之間策劃起事，一八二〇年一月一日在塞維亞城外的「卡維薩斯營地」率所部宣告國王必須宣誓遵從一八一二年憲法；一月二十日他出任陸軍部長，把一次營房起義變成全國性的政治運動。安達盧西亞總司令奧賴利伯爵選擇服從，避免了流血；加的斯與巴塞羅那亦先後響應，後者迫使蒙茹伊克城堡的守將維加伯爵繳械退讓。自由派最重要的軍事人物是弗朗西斯科·埃斯波斯·伊·米納：一八一三年起在納瓦拉山區以游擊抗法，一八二〇年再度起義並組建「內陸軍」，一八二二年出任陸軍部長並一度以攝政身分主持國政，同時以游擊隊牽制正統派的反攻。西班牙自由派自一八二二年起分裂為溫和的立憲派與激進的單一制派，前者以米格爾·德·阿古埃列斯等法學家與將領為代表。與之對立的是斐迪南七世與其妻瑪麗亞·伊莎貝爾所代表的正統派核心，宮廷樞密與主教在幕後策劃；一八二二年七月七日正是在皇室衛隊軍官帶動下發生反攻，十月國王下令排除五十二名立憲派人士。
peopleEn: The man who lit the fuse was Rafael del Riego, a Galician who had first been imprisoned in 1808 for opposing the French invasion and who became known in the army for his outspokenness. He plotted among officers from 1819 to 1820 and on 1 January 1820 proclaimed, at the Campo de las Cabezas outside Seville, that the king must swear to the Constitution of 1812; on 20 January he became minister of war and turned a barracks rising into a national political movement. The captain-general of Andalusia, the Count of O'Reilly, chose submission and so avoided bloodshed; Cadiz and Barcelona answered in turn, the latter forcing the governor of the Montjuic citadel, the Count of Vigo, to hand over his guns. The most important soldier of the constitutional side was Francisco Espoz y Mina: from 1813 he had fought the French in the mountains of Navarre as a partisan, rose again in 1820 and built the Interior Army, became minister of war in 1822 and briefly presided over the state as regent, and at the same time used his bands to pin down the royalist counter-offensive. From 1822 the Spanish liberals split into the moderate constitutionalists and the radical unitarians, the former represented by jurists and officers such as Miguel de Arguelles. Against them stood the absolutist core of Fernando VII and of his wife Maria Isabel de Bourbon, with the privy councillors and the bishops plotting behind the scenes; on 7 July 1822 it was officers of the Royal Guard who led the counter-stroke, and in October the king ordered the exclusion of fifty-two constitutionalists.
kits: 卡面這件一七一〇年的燧發槍，正好是西班牙軍隊在拿破崙戰爭年代到一八二三年之間的標準步槍：英國在一七〇〇年代後期定型的「褐貝絲」型燧發線槍，口徑約十四點六毫米並配刺刀，是西班牙線列步兵在半島戰爭中大量接收的英國援助裝備，軍中同時雜有國產的「溫莎型」一八一五年製燧發槍；到一八二〇年，軍械庫裡既有新式燧發槍，也有上一代剩餘的火繩槍，守城與攻城的時候兩種都上肩。立憲派民兵與義勇兵的裝備更雜：城防砲兵用的仍是老式攻城砲與騎兵砲，義勇兵則自備獵槍、卡賓槍與散彈槍，數百人手中只有短管的獵槍，追擊與守夜靠的是槍上的刺刀而不是精準的瞄準。正統派的山區武裝則多靠走私：巴斯克沿岸的走私者把英國與美國的燧發槍由聖塞瓦斯蒂安與畢爾巴鄂偷運入山，躲開關卡交給各村的游擊隊使用。法軍一八二三年遠征的裝備是法軍自己的國制野砲連：四磅、六磅與八磅騎兵砲隨步兵行進，另有十二磅攻城砲與工程器材，砲車靠騾隊與牛車拖行，給養在行軍途中向沿線村鎮徵收，馬匹大量病死與掉隊。法國人還把一批英製燧發槍改發給西班牙的歸順部隊，使西班牙軍隊短時間內成了法式火器與英式火器混裝的樣子。西班牙自己的火藥產能有限，塞哥維亞與阿拉瓦的火藥廠供應全軍，銅料與鐵料仍仰給外省，軍械修理多靠民間鐵匠。
kitsEn: The flintlock musket of 1710 on this card was exactly the standard musket of the Spanish army between the Napoleonic wars and 1823: the Brown Bess type flintlock musket, standardised in Britain in the early eighteenth century at about 14.6 mm calibre and fitted with a bayonet, was the British military aid equipment that the Spanish line infantry received in large quantity during the Peninsular War, and the service also held a mixture of home-made Windsor pattern flintlock muskets of 1815; by 1820 the arsenals held new flintlocks and the previous generation's matchlocks side by side, and both went to the shoulder when men were put into the trench. The equipment of the constitutionalist militias was far more chaotic: the old siege guns and horse pieces of the artillery parks were still in service, while the volunteers brought their own hunting guns, carbines and shot guns, and hundreds of men carried nothing but short-barrelled fowling pieces, so that what sustained them in pursuit and in the night watch was the bayonet on the gun rather than any aiming. The royalist bands in the mountains depended largely on smuggling: the smugglers along the Basque coast ran British and American flintlocks past the customs posts at San Sebastian and Bilbao and handed them to the village bands. The equipment of the French expedition of 1823 was their own national artillery park: four-, six- and eight-pounder horse guns marched with the infantry, with twelve-pounder siege guns and engineer stores besides, the gun carriages hauled by mule teams and ox-carts, the food taken from the villages along the march, and a great many horses sickened or strayed. The French in 1823 also distributed a batch of British-made flintlocks to the Spanish units that had gone over, so that for a short time the Spanish army wore a mixture of French ordnance and British ordnance. Spanish output of gunpowder was limited, the factories at Segovia and Alava supplying the whole army, while copper and iron still came from the provinces and the repairs of weapons were left to village smiths.
tactics: 一八二〇年的關鍵不在會戰，而在「pronunciamiento」這種西班牙式舉事：軍官率營兵進城，在廣場舉起一八一二年憲法，宣讀並要求國王當眾宣誓，城市的國民警衛隊與街上市眾是否跟從，決定舉事成敗；火砲站在哪一邊往往比幾百支步槍更要緊。一月一日塞維亞，拉斐爾·德·列戈帶約二千人自城外的「卡維薩斯營地」開進市區，守軍與市長不加抵抗；一月八日巴塞羅那宣告，一月二十一日蒙茹伊克城堡的守軍在火砲威脅下繳械；二月六日馬德里市區起義，街上築起街壘，國王三月九日被迫宣誓遵從一八一二年憲法。此後的形勢是「內戰中的內戰」：一八二二年七月七日皇室衛隊反攻，摧毀馬德里的自由派街壘，立憲派中央政府瓦解；十二月起阿拉貢的卡爾塔尤德爆發正統派起義，自由派以圍剿消耗其兵力，一八二三年三月法軍開到前線又迫使雙方停火。自由派在山區的戰術是游擊：埃斯波斯·伊·米納的隊伍穿白色襯衫以免夜間誤傷，專打法軍的小隊、輜重與郵隊，切斷從法國邊境通往馬德里的糧道；加塔隆尼亞的米拉恩斯·德爾·博斯克在海岸山區同日運作。一八二三年法軍的戰術相反：主力縱隊晝夜行軍，騎兵前哨警戒，宿營先挖壕再列陣，避免與西班牙零散部隊糾纏，專以限期投降迫令城市就範；四月二十一日在米拉戈薩以一次會戰擊潰薩爾斯菲爾德部，五月二十日兵不血刃進入馬德里，靠的是人數與士氣而不是攻城術。
tacticsEn: The key of 1820 was not a pitched battle but the pronunciamiento, the Spanish form of insurrection: an officer marched his battalion into the city, raised the Constitution of 1812 in the square, read it out and demanded that the king swear to it in public, and whether the city militia and the crowds followed decided whether the rising succeeded; which side the guns stood on often mattered more than a few hundred muskets. On 1 January in Seville, Rafael del Riego brought about two thousand men in from the Campo de las Cabezas outside the city, and neither the garrison nor the mayor offered resistance; Barcelona declared itself on 8 January, and on 21 January the garrison of the Montjuic citadel gave up its guns under the threat of the artillery; on 6 February the capital rose and barricades were thrown up in the streets, and the king was forced to swear the Constitution of 1812 on 9 March. What followed was a civil war inside a civil war: on 7 July 1822 the Royal Guard counter-attacked and destroyed the liberal barricades in Madrid, and the constitutional government in the capital collapsed; from December the royalists rose at Calatayud in Aragon, and the constitutionalists wore them down in a series of sieges, which the arrival of the French in March 1823 then froze. The constitutional tactics in the mountains were those of the partisan: Espoz y Mina's men wore white shirts so as not to shoot each other by night, and struck only the French detachments, the baggage trains and the mail, cutting the food road that ran from the French border to Madrid; in Catalonia Francisco Milans del Bosch worked the same way along the coastal mountains. The French tactics of 1823 were the opposite: the main column marched day and night, cavalry outposts kept watch, and each camp was dug into before it was formed, so as not to be entangled with the scattered Spanish bands; they preferred to bring cities to terms within a fixed period rather than storm them, and on 21 April a single pitched battle at La Milagrosa broke Sarsfield's troops, after which the army entered Madrid on 20 May without a shot, on the strength of numbers and morale rather than siegecraft.
data: 留下數字的地方不多，而且雙方戰報都往自己一方添水分。一八二〇年一月一日塞維亞起事，拉斐爾·德·列戈帶出的營兵與士兵約二千至三千人，這是全歐自由派運動中規模最小、影響最大的一次舉事。西班牙一八二〇年的常備軍約三萬至四萬人，國民警衛隊在一八一四年被解散、一八二〇年三月才恢復重建，實際能上陣者遠低於法定人數；一八一二年被推翻的「弒君者」共五十二人，一八一五年十月七日被絞死於馬德里特雷亞諾的葡萄園。一八二二年十月國王下令排除的五十二名立憲派人士是第二批，與前一批數目相同。一八二三年法國遠征軍由維羅納會議批准十萬人，實際集結並裝備的約八萬人，四月越過比達索阿河進入西班牙者約五萬至六萬人，隨軍火砲近百門；法軍自四月十三日過境到五月二十日進入馬德里，用了三十七天走約四百五十公里，途中因給養不足與掉隊而減員甚多。西班牙方面在法軍抵達前已整師倒向國王，陣亡與被俘者以數百計，四月二十一日米拉戈薩之戰是西班牙軍中最重的一次損失。馬德里人口約十二至十五萬，全國人口約一千二百萬。拉斐爾·德·列戈於一八二三年十一月七日與五十餘名同伴在馬德里「塞瓦達廣場」被絞死。卡面那件一七一〇年的燧發槍沒有可比的數字，它決定的是每分鐘的發射數與單發命中率，而不是戰役的規模。
dataEn: Figures survive only in scattered form, and both sides' reports inflated their own. On 1 January 1820 at Seville, Riego took out perhaps two to three thousand soldiers and men of his battalion, the smallest rising in Europe with the largest consequences. The standing army of Spain in 1820 numbered roughly thirty to forty thousand men; the National Militia had been dissolved in 1814 and was only restored in March 1820, and far fewer than its legal complement could be brought into the field; the fifty-two regicides overthrown before the Constitution of 1812 were hanged at the vineyard of the Triano in Madrid on 7 October 1815. The fifty-two constitutionalists excluded by the king in October 1822 were the second batch, equal in number to the first. The French expedition of 1823 was authorised by the Congress of Verona at a hundred thousand men; some eighty thousand were assembled and equipped, and between fifty and sixty thousand actually crossed the Bidasoa into Spain in April with close to a hundred guns; the French took thirty-seven days to cover about four hundred and fifty kilometres from the crossing on 13 April to Madrid on 20 May, with heavy losses from want of food and from stragglers on the march. The Spanish units had already gone over to the king in whole regiments before the French arrived, and their killed and captured ran to hundreds, the heaviest single loss of the Spanish army falling at La Milagrosa on 21 April. Madrid had a population of roughly one hundred and twenty to one hundred and fifty thousand, and the country some twelve million. Riego was hanged at the Plaza de la Cebada in Madrid on 7 November 1823 together with more than fifty of his companions. The flintlock musket of 1710 on the card has no comparable figure to offer: what it decided was the rate of fire per minute and the hit rate of a single shot, not the scale of the campaign.
cause: 打起上來有遠因，也有近因。遠因是拿破崙入侵西班牙：在一八〇八至一八一四年的半島戰爭中，西班牙軍民在沒有國王的情況下自行組織洪都拉斯，一八一二年的《加的斯憲法》正是這場全民抗戰的政治產物。一八一三年六月二十一日維多利亞一役，英葡聯軍在威靈頓指揮下擊潰法軍主力，次年斐迪南七世復位，卻把戰時建立的自由制度全部推翻：廢除一八一二年憲法、恢復宗教裁判所、絞死五十二名「弒君者」、查禁共濟會與學生聯會、封閉大學。國家的經濟同時塌陷：美洲殖民地相繼獨立，白銀與海運貿易斷絕，軍費無著；一八一七年至一八一九年接連歉收，糧價飛漲，城市手工業者與軍人家庭受苦最深，而王朝廷廷仍維持一八一四年復辟時的奢靡開支，於是軍中與城市裡反對專制的人越來越多。近因是一八二〇年初王室決定再派遠征軍赴美洲收復殖民地，出征準備不足、士氣低落，軍官之間的密謀在一八一九年已被安全當局破獲，幾名主謀被判重刑，這反而逼出更急迫的行動；拉斐爾·德·列戈原計劃在聖誕節夜間起事，因準備未妥而延至一月一日，隨即引發全國連鎖響應。
causeEn: There were remote causes and immediate ones. The remote cause was the invasion of Spain by Napoleon: in the Peninsular War of 1808 to 1814 the Spanish people organised juntas without a king, and the Constitution of Cadiz of 1812 was the political product of that whole-nation resistance. On 21 June 1813 the allies won the battle of Vitoria under Wellington and broke the main French army; Fernando VII returned in 1814 and threw away every institution built during the war: he abolished the Constitution of 1812, restored the Inquisition, hanged the fifty-two regicides, banned the masonic lodges and the student unions and closed the universities. The economy collapsed at the same time: the American colonies declared independence one after another, the silver and the sea trade were cut off, and there was no money for the army; the harvests failed in 1817, 1818 and 1819, grain prices soared, and the urban artisans and the soldiers' families bore the worst of it, while the royal household kept the extravagant expenditure of the restoration, so that the number of people in the army and in the cities opposed to absolutism kept growing. The immediate cause lay in the decision of the court in the early months of 1820 to send another expedition to the Americas to recover the colonies: the troops were unprepared and morale was low, the conspiracy among officers had already been broken up in 1819 and its leaders sentenced, which only drove them to a more desperate step; Riego had intended to rise on Christmas night, but the preparations were not ready and the movement slipped to 1 January, and from that moment the chain reaction ran through the whole country.
impact: 這場革命的第一層影響在西班牙體制內：三年的立憲時期把「洪都拉斯」這種城市自治、國民警衛隊與議會政治引入國家生活，一八二一年在塞維利亞通過的新憲法更試圖用攝政與兩院制取代一八一二年憲法的原始民主色彩。第二層在國際：維羅納會議同意法國干預，等於把一八一五年維也納體系最核心的「正統主義」原則從防禦轉為進攻工具，英國外相卡寧與威靈頓的拒絕使干預失去多國背書，反而坐實「法國要獨自支配西班牙」的說法；葡屬巴西的獨立運動與南美洲各解放軍的節節勝利，也因西班牙自身捲入內戰而加速。一八二〇年後西班牙自由派政府曾再派遠征軍赴美洲，此後大批軍官與學生隨玻利瓦爾、聖馬丁的隊伍渡海，其中一批人後來回到西班牙，成為一八二六年前後流亡派武裝的骨幹。第三層最為長遠：一八二三年之後的「大獵巫」把自由派驅入地下，王室在復辟後依然以一八一四年廢除憲法的法令為唯一合法來源，這種拒絕承認任何憲政契約的立場，正是日後卡爾斯派在斐迪南七世一八三三年去世時舉起「合法王位」旗號的根由；一八二三年法國干預也留下一個可被反覆援引的先例，歐洲此後每一次自由派起義，都要重新計算干預的代價。
impactEn: The first layer of the revolution's effect lay inside Spain: three years of constitutional government introduced into national life such things as the city junta, the National Militia and parliamentary politics, and the new constitution passed at Seville in 1821 tried to replace the raw democratic colour of the Constitution of 1812 with a regency and two chambers. The second layer was international. The Congress of Verona agreeing to a French intervention turned the principle of legitimacy at the heart of the Vienna settlement of 1815 from a defence into an instrument of attack; the refusal of the British foreign secretary Canning and of Wellington stripped the intervention of any multinational backing and confirmed the charge that France meant to dominate Spain by herself. The independence of Portuguese Brazil and the advancing victories of the South American liberators were quickened by Spain's own entanglement in civil war. After 1820 the Spanish liberal government sent another expedition to the Americas, and afterwards large numbers of officers and students crossed the sea with Bolivar and San Martin; a number of them returned to Spain later and formed the backbone of the exiled armed groups of the mid-1820s. The third layer proved the most durable: the Great Hunt after 1823 drove the liberals underground, and the restored court still treated the decree abolishing the constitution of 1814 as its sole title to legitimacy, and this refusal to acknowledge any constitutional compact is precisely the root of the Carlist rising of 1833, when they raised the banner of the legitimate king at Fernando VII's death; the French intervention of 1823 also left a precedent that could be cited again and again, and every later liberal rising in Europe had afterwards to weigh the cost of intervention.
result: 結果分兩截。一八二〇年的起事成功：國王斐迪南七世於三月九日在馬德里宣誓遵從一八一二年憲法，拉斐爾·德·列戈出任陸軍部長，各省洪都拉斯取得實際自治，國民警衛隊重新組建；一八二一年自由派還在塞維利亞通過一部新憲法，並計劃擴大徵兵與整頓軍隊。但聯盟很快瓦解：一八二二年七月七日皇室衛隊在馬德里反攻，立憲派政府垮台，國王在十月清洗五十二名立憲派人士；十二月起正統派在阿拉貢的卡爾塔尤德起義，內戰全面化。一八二三年法國出兵：四月十三日過境，四月二十一日米拉戈薩會戰，隨即沿大道南下，所到之處西班牙各團多數整師歸順，五月二十日法軍進入馬德里，攝政政府退往加的斯與海灣各地，十月簽訂停戰協議，法軍主力撤回法國，自由派大批流亡，海外僅存一個「西班牙自由派」的組織。一八二三年十一月七日拉斐爾·德·列戈與五十餘名同伴在馬德里的塞瓦達廣場被絞死，一八一五年那齣戲在西班牙又重演一次。卡面這件兵器在此役中沒有決定任何一場勝負：決定馬德里陷落的是法軍的人數、騎兵與大砲，是西班牙軍隊在關鍵時刻的倒戈，以及維羅納會議背後的外交安排；燧發槍的任務是讓一八二〇年街頭的民兵能連續射擊，讓一八二二年守夜的國民警衛隊在城頭撐住，讓一八二三年的游擊隊伏擊小股敵軍——它決定的是每一排步槍手在那一刻的士氣，而不是國家的命運。
resultEn: The outcome came in two instalments. The rising of 1820 succeeded: on 9 March Fernando VII swore the Constitution of 1812 in Madrid, Riego became minister of war, the provincial juntas acquired real autonomy, and the National Militia was reconstituted; in 1821 the liberals even passed a new constitution at Seville and planned to enlarge the conscription and reorganise the army. But the alliance soon broke down: on 7 July 1822 the Royal Guard counter-attacked in Madrid, the constitutional government fell, and in October the king purged fifty-two constitutionalists; from December the royalists rose at Calatayud in Aragon and the civil war became general. France came in 1823: crossing the frontier on 13 April, winning the battle of La Milagrosa on 21 April and then marching down the main road, it was met almost everywhere by Spanish regiments that went over whole, and the French entered Madrid on 20 May, while the regency government withdrew to Cadiz and the other ports of the bay; in October an armistice was signed and the main body of the French army returned to France, with the liberals exiled in large numbers and their organisation abroad surviving only as a society of Spanish liberals. On 7 November 1823 Rafael del Riego and more than fifty of his companions were hanged at the Plaza de la Cebada in Madrid, and the drama of 1815 was acted out again in Spain. The weapon on the card decided no battle in this war: what brought Madrid down was the French numbers, cavalry and heavy guns, the defection of the Spanish army at the decisive moment, and the diplomatic settlement behind the Congress of Verona; the musket's task was to let the urban militia of 1820 keep firing in the streets, to hold the National Militia on the walls through the night watch of 1822, and to arm the partisans of 1823 for their ambushes; it decided the morale of each rank of musketeers at the moment of firing, not the fate of the state.
